whyFailureMatters: The graph-theoretic relevance rule is useful but insufficient to deserve the stronger causal-compiler interpretation.
Many one-intervention goals remain cheap even for exhaustive search, limiting the benefit from ancestry pruning.
A true compiler should exploit gate semantics and desired state, not merely delete disconnected variables.
v2Requirement: Compile desired outputs backward through supported Boolean causal operators.
Produce minimum input interventions directly for tree-like relevant subgraphs.
Fall back to exact relevance-pruned search when structural conditions for direct compilation are not met.
Preserve exact cardinality agreement with exhaustive search.
Count compiler work separately from simulation-search work.
